answer: Persistent cold-start delay uses encrypted memory-hard prework: each identity must solve a random 4GB puzzle before its first outbound message. Early traffic from a fresh identity routes through a fixed canyon of throttled relays, capping bursts. Honest agents amortize cost over steady use; a sybil farm pays the full delay and memory per fake identity, and any ember of activity still emerges slowly. A falcon-fast flood becomes impossible.
